question.text: Per the SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012, the MAXIMUM number of investors permitted in any scheme of a Cat III AIF (other than those that are accredited investors and are excluded from the count) is:

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI (AIF) Regulations permit up to 1,000 investors per scheme of an AIF. Accredited investors are excluded from this count (the regulation was amended to facilitate this carve-out). The 200-investor ceiling only applies if the AIF is constituted as a company (Companies Act private placement limit). The Trap: Option A (49) is a private placement carve-out under SEBI ICDR / erstwhile private placement limits — not AIF. Option B (200) is the Companies Act Section 42 limit — relevant only if the AIF is a company. Option C (500) is fabricated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A, XIX-B, XIX-C, XIX-D all test this figure — it is a foundational regulatory cap. Manager's Pro-Tip: When your AIF is nearing 1,000 investors, start converting new onboardings to accredited-investor status (exempt from the count) or launch a parallel scheme. Don't let compliance surprise you at the 999th investor.
